question: A company needs an automation solution that enforces the desired state of the infrastructure and automatically reverts any manual configuration changes. The solution will initially be used for network devices but must later extend to server infrastructure as well. Which tool meets these requirements?
explanation: Community vote is split near-evenly between C (Puppet) and D; Puppet's agent-based enforcement of desired state (with automatic drift correction) matches the requirement described.
theory: Puppet's agent periodically pulls a compiled manifest from a puppet master and reconciles the live system against it, automatically correcting any manual configuration drift back to the desired state; the same agent/master model (via the Open Agent Container on supported Nexus platforms) works for both network devices and traditional servers, making it a natural fit when the requirement explicitly needs both continuous enforcement and eventual server-side reuse. Ansible is push/on-demand rather than continuously enforcing, and raw Python/Bash scripts have no built-in state-reconciliation model at all. (Cisco documentation / web research)
